title: Quill Health — outbound + partnership scratch notebook
content:
Notes to self — Quill Health (digital-first chronic care management)

Why Quill? quick hypothesis:
- Heavy on clinical triage + longitudinal notes -> lots of short & medium prompts (summaries, intake, triage recommendations).
- Must keep PHI private; likely will require Private deployment (VPC/HSM) or strict hosted controls + BAA.
- Early-stage ML infra (internal infra team small) — they want turnkey inference with predictable latency for clinical workflows.
- Could convert a convo-to-summary path into huge token cost if not cached/quantized. Opportunity: reduce cost while meeting 250–500ms SLO for triage path.

Primary personas to target (sequence order):
1) Head of Clinical Innovation — cares about outcomes, clinician UX, hallucination risk, validation/certainty.
2) ML/Platform Lead — cares about runtime, quantization, integration, deployment modes (dedicated vs private), model ops.
3) CTO / VP Eng — security, contracts (BAA), SLA, long term vendor risk.
4) Product manager for Care Ops — will be power user for metrics, evals, rollouts.

Account intelligence (public + hints):
- Based in US East, raised Series B in 2024, recently announced partnerships with two telehealth networks (press release Nov 2024).
- Hiring: job posts for "ML infra engineer" and "clinical data engineer" — implies on-prem-ish needs but limited headcount.
- Their product demo shows 1–1 clinician workflows and batch analytics.
- Regulatory: working with HIPAA-covered payors; quotes on their page about "patient data security".

Key pain signals to surface in outreach:
- "We're seeing latency spikes during peak triage windows"
- "Costs balloon with long clinical note generation"
- "Need verifiable audit trails and access controls for PHI"
- "Want canary + rollback for model updates to avoid clinical regressions"

Quick outbound play (6-touch multichannel):
Touch 1 — Email (subject A/B):
  A: "Pilot idea — reduce triage latency + token cost for Quill Health"
  B: "Short note: how Quill can keep PHI private and speed clinician workflows"
  Body (short): 1–2 lines of personalization (mention telehealth partner), 1 sentence value prop (dedicated inference + quantization profiles -> 30–60% token cost reduction), 1 social proof (startup X cut cost 45% + met 200ms SLO), CTA: quick 15-min sync to share pilot plan.

Touch 2 — LinkedIn InMail / connection + POV comment on their blog post (2 days later)
Touch 3 — Follow-up email with one-pager attachment (pilot outline + TCO comparison) (4 days)
Touch 4 — Call / voicemail to Head of Clinical Innovation (if number available) — call script snippet below
Touch 5 — Slack/Email to engineering alias (if found) with technical one-pager and offer for bench trial (dedicated small cluster for 30 days)
Touch 6 — Exec outreach (CTO) with contract-level notes + BAA ping (if still hot)

Draft email (TO: Head of Clinical Innovation) — quick scratch:
Subject: Pilot proposal — faster triage + cheaper notes for Quill
Hi {{firstName}},

Saw Quill's recent collaboration with [telehealth-partner] — congrats. Quick thought: we helped a similar care team reduce per-note inference cost ~40% while keeping generation latency <300ms using a mix of prefix cache + model variant routing. If there's appetite, I'd love to propose a 6-week pilot (low risk) to validate on a small triage flow and hand over a config that scales to production.

15 minutes next week to share a short plan?

— Maya

A/B test notes: try pricing-focused subject vs clinical outcome-focused subject; measure reply rate and meeting conversion.

Call script (30s hook -> 3 discovery questions -> next step):
- Hook: "Quick note — we built an inference config that cut triage latency and token spend for a chronic care team by ~40% without changing model outputs."
- Q1 (product fit): "Which clinician flows generate the most notes today?"
- Q2 (scale): "What's your current monthly token volume estimate for triage & intake?"
- Q3 (security): "Are you able to host inference in a VPC/HSM today or would a Redwood Private instance be required?"
- Close: propose a 1–2 week bench test on a small dataset or a 15-min architecture review.

Objection handling cheatsheet (short bullets):
- "We can't send PHI to a third-party": Redwood Private option + BAA + customer-managed KMS — offer network diagram and SOC2/HIPAA docs.
- "Costs look high": show TCO comparison (hosted + dedicated + quantized onto cheaper GPUs) — propose staged plan (bench -> pilot -> dedicated).
- "We need accuracy guarantees": agree to eval on our test set + create clinician L0 metrics (precision of suggested triage actions) — run blind evals.
- "Too many vendor integrations": propose minimal API shim (1–2 endpoints) and a data-sampling plan for first 30 days.

Pilot skeleton (6-week):
- Week 0: scoping + data access + NDA/BAA; define 3–5 prompts & acceptance metric
- Week 1–2: bench trial on non-PHI sampled data or synthetic PHI; performance profiling (latency/cost/quality)
- Week 3–4: small production canary (dedicated pool vs hosted) — measure SLOs + clinician feedback
- Week 5: rollout config + training handoff + runbook for rollbacks
- Week 6: results + TCO + rollout recommendation (canary plan)

Success metrics to propose early:
- 95th percentile latency <= 400ms for triage path (target 250–300ms)
- Token cost per note reduced by >= 30% vs baseline
- Clinician acceptance rate of generated summaries >= 85% in blind eval
- No data exfiltration — pass security checklist + log audit review

Pricing thought (scratch):
- Offer 3 flavors for pilot quote: hosted-limited (cheapest, limited retention), dedicated-sandbox (moderate, predictable throughput), private-vpc (highest, full-control).
- For pilot: flat $5k–10kish testing fee + cost reimbursement for infra (cap $4k) — keep it simple for early stage.

Open questions / TODOs (internal):
- Validate exact telehealth partner name (press release ambiguous) — Ethan to confirm via LinkedIn.
- Check legal for BAA template and an example MSA amendment for private deploy (Leah).
- Build a short demo dataset generator that creates 500 synthetic triage notes (to avoid PHI) — engineer ask: 2d effort.
- Prepare 1-pager TCO table (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with realistic token assumptions for triage flows.

Potential red flags / deal-killers:
- They already built internal inference pipeline and have strict vendor lock policies (unlikely but possible).
- Extremely low monthly spend (under $1k) — not worth dedicated setup.

Competitor mapping (brief):
- Vendor A: cheaper but no private deploy / limited audit logs.
- Vendor B: enterprise-only, long legal cycles, slower time to pilot.

Next steps (this week):
- [ ] Draft outbound email + A/B subjects (Maya)
- [ ] Confirm telehealth partner name + any mentionable wins (Ethan)
- [ ] Legal check for BAA + pilot SOW template (Leah)
- [ ] Prototype synthetic data generator (ask infra bench team)

Notes to self: keep outreach lightweight and clinically-focused; avoid deep infra talk on first touch. If they reply, route to Leah + engineering for architecture review.

Scratchy brainstorm (for demo storytelling):
- Use a 3-part narrative: (1) clinician sees faster summary in EHR, (2) system suggests triage urgency with confidence band, (3) logs for audit + rollback on model version.
- Visual: show before/after token counts, cost per week, and latency waterfall (tokenization -> model -> postprocessing).

— end of notebook —

(Short-term archive tag: outreach-2026-q1)
